subject: Reliability brief: storage GC regression & QBR action roster
messages:
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reliability brief: storage GC regression & QBR action roster

Team —

Quick brief ahead of next week’s QBR prep: we experienced a short but visible throughput regression on our hosted region (us-west-2) during the overnight window on 2026-11-12. High-level:
- Incident window: ~2026-11-12 23:42 — 2026-11-13 00:00 PST (18 minutes).
- Symptom: P95 token latency increased ~2.2x for impacted requests; error rate briefly spiked to ~1.1%.
- Initial triage: storage metadata GC spike on a subset of metadata servers correlated with a config rollout earlier that day.
- Customer impact: several high-throughput customers saw transient tail-latency; one tier-2 customer (Acme) logged a support case.

Attached: incident_timeline_v1.pdf (draft) and the raw support transcript from Acme.

Ask: I need a one-page executive summary + action roster for the QBR. Please reply with owners for the items below by EOD today so I can consolidate:
A) Root-cause summary and permanent mitigation plan (owner + ETA)
B) Customer outreach language + credit/compensation recommendation (owner)
C) Monitoring/dashboard changes and alerting tuning (owner)
D) Postmortem write-up owner and publish ETA

I started a skeleton exec one-pager (exec_one_pager_draft.md) — please add in-line or attach your version.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Lead, Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reliability brief: storage GC regression & QBR action roster

Thanks Marissa — good catch and good timing to lock this down before QBR. Quick notes from infra triage:
- Preliminary root cause: recent metadata-config rollout lowered compaction/GC thresholds to reduce disk usage; under high concurrent shard activity this triggered longer GC pauses on 4/22 metadata nodes which cascaded into increased KV lookup latencies.
- Immediate mitigation taken: rollback that flag (rolled back at 00:12 PST) and increased metadata GC threshold for the short term.

Proposed owners:
A) Root-cause & permanent fix: Vivek (owner) — ETA: 2026-11-30 for a targeted config + automated pre-flight checks.
B) Customer outreach + credits: Marcus (owner) — propose standard 5% monthly credit for impacted billing period unless legal/finance advise otherwise.
C) Monitoring/alerting: Hannah (owner) — add a GC pause metric to the P95 latency dashboard and create an automated synthetic test. ETA: 2026-11-20.
D) Postmortem: Marissa (owner) to draft; engineering to provide logs. Publish ETA: 2026-11-22.

I recommend we include a short bullet on prevented recurrence (pre-flight config gates) in the QBR slide. Also recommend a brief note to affected customers that we rolled back and are tracking further steps.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Tim Owens <tim.owens@acme.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reliability brief: storage GC regression & QBR action roster

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up. We saw a burst of 500ms+ tails across several of our endpoints during the window; it caused a few user-facing slowdowns for our customers. Our team collected traces and attached them to our ticket (see acme_support_transcript.txt). Two quick asks from our side:
1) Can you confirm whether this is a one-off from a config change or something we should expect to see again?
2) Will Redwood propose a credit/compensation (we've flagged this on our billing review) and can you share the ETA for the permanent fix?

Appreciate the transparency — we’ll reference your QBR note in our internal review.

Tim
Tim Owens
Director, Platform Ops
Acme Corp

[Draft customer note]
Hi Tim — thanks again for flagging this. We identified a metadata GC threshold change as the proximate cause; we rolled back the flag within 30 minutes of detection which restored normal P95 within ~6 minutes of the rollback. Our recommendations: temporary credit of 5% for the impacted billing period and a permanent fix (config gate + automated pre-flight) with ETA 2026-11-30. We will follow up with the postmortem by 2026-11-22.

Action roster (current):
- Vivek: permanent mitigation design + pre-flight checks (ETA 2026-11-30)
- Marcus: customer communication + compensation proposal (ETA 2026-11-18) — draft language above
- Hannah: monitoring/dashboard + synthetic test (ETA 2026-11-20)
- Marissa: postmortem draft + QBR slide (ETA 2026-11-22)

Please confirm these owners/dates or propose alternates. Marcus — can you own the outreach to Acme? If you want legal/finance looped in I can add them to the reply.

Marissa
